system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
The Hearthline T4 (HL-T4, Rev. C) is a Wi-Fi, wall-mounted programmable thermostat controlled by its dial, the Hearthline app (iOS 15+/Android 10+) or voice assistants. It works with all common heating systems: 24 V boilers and furnaces, single-stage heat pumps, and line-voltage electric heaters such as baseboards; multi-stage heat pumps need the HL-RM2 relay module. It runs off a C-wire or the supplied adapter kit, with two AA lithium batteries backing up the display and schedule for up to 12 months (they cannot run the heating). It connects over 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz Wi-Fi with WPA2/WPA3-Personal; Bluetooth is for setup only. You can set up to eight temperature periods a day, with a different schedule for each weekday, between 5 °C and 32 °C in half-degree steps; frost protection holds 5 °C when off. Geofencing needs app 3.2+ and "Always" location access. Up to four remote sensors can be paired and averaged. Firmware auto-installs overnight (02:00–04:00) unless manual updates are switched on; security patches always install. It is indoor-only, 0–40 °C. The warranty is two years, or three if registered in the app within 30 days.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
PRODUCT SPECIFICATION — HEARTHLINE T4 SMART THERMOSTAT (Model HL-T4, Rev. C)

Overview. The Hearthline T4 is a wall-mounted programmable thermostat with Wi-Fi connectivity, designed for residential central heating and cooling systems. It is controlled from the front-panel dial, the Hearthline app (iOS 15+ and Android 10+), or supported voice assistants.

System compatibility. The T4 is compatible with 24 V AC low-voltage systems, including gas, oil and LPG boilers with a volt-free or 24 V control input, conventional forced-air furnaces, and single-stage heat pumps. It is NOT compatible with line-voltage (120 V or 230 V) systems, such as electric baseboard heaters and storage heaters, which must not be wired to the unit. Multi-stage heat pumps require the optional HL-RM2 relay module (sold separately).

Power. The unit is powered from the C-wire (common wire) where present. Where no C-wire is available, the included power adapter kit must be fitted at the boiler or furnace. Two AA lithium batteries provide backup power for the display and schedule memory for up to 12 months; the heating relay will not operate on battery power alone.

Connectivity. Wi-Fi: IEEE 802.11 b/g/n, 2.4 GHz band only. 5 GHz networks are not supported; on dual-band routers the 2.4 GHz band must be enabled during setup. WPA2 and WPA3-Personal security are supported; enterprise (802.1X) networks are not. Bluetooth LE 5.0 is used for initial setup only.

Scheduling. Up to six (6) temperature periods per day may be set, with separate schedules for each day of the week. Setpoint range is 5 °C to 32 °C in 0.5 °C increments. A frost-protection setpoint of 5 °C applies whenever the unit is switched to Off. Geofencing (automatic away mode based on phone location) requires app version 3.2 or later and location permission set to "Always".

Sensors. Built-in temperature sensor accuracy is ±0.3 °C between 10 °C and 30 °C. Humidity sensor accuracy is ±3% RH. Up to four HL-RS1 remote room sensors can be paired; when remote sensors are used, the unit averages readings from the sensors selected for each schedule period.

Firmware. Firmware updates are downloaded and installed automatically between 02:00 and 04:00 local time, unless the user has enabled "Manual updates" in the app, in which case the user is notified and must approve each update. Security patches are installed automatically regardless of this setting.

Environment. Operating temperature 0 °C to 40 °C; relative humidity 10–90%, non-condensing. For indoor use only. Do not install in bathrooms (zone 0–2) or in direct sunlight.

Dimensions and weight. 86 mm × 86 mm × 24 mm; 145 g without batteries.

Warranty. Two (2) years from date of purchase. The warranty is extended to three (3) years if the product is registered in the Hearthline app within 30 days of purchase. Warranty does not cover damage caused by installation on incompatible systems.

Installation. Hearthline recommends installation by a qualified heating engineer. Mains-powered adapter kits must be fitted by a qualified electrician in the UK and EU.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. How long will the AA batteries keep the schedule memory alive if power is lost?
2. My flat is heated by 230 V electric baseboard heaters. Can I fit the T4 to control them?
3. My mesh router only broadcasts a 5 GHz network. Will the thermostat connect to it?
4. I want seven temperature changes on weekdays (wake, leave, lunch, return, evening, late, night). Can the T4 do that?
response:
Checking against the specification itself, my earlier notes were wrong on three of these four points. The answers below come from the document.

**1. Battery backup: up to 12 months.**
The two AA lithium batteries keep the display and schedule memory alive for up to 12 months. They won't run the heating, because the heating relay doesn't operate on battery power alone.

**2. 230 V electric baseboard heaters: no, do not fit it.**
My notes said line-voltage heaters were supported. That was wrong. The T4 only works with 24 V AC low-voltage systems. The spec explicitly says it is not compatible with line-voltage (120 V or 230 V) systems such as electric baseboard and storage heaters, and these "must not be wired to the unit." Wiring it anyway is dangerous, and the warranty doesn't cover damage from installation on incompatible systems. You'll need a thermostat rated for line voltage.

**3. 5 GHz-only mesh router: no, it won't connect.**
My notes said 5 GHz was supported. That was also wrong. The T4 uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only (802.11 b/g/n), and 5 GHz networks are not supported. Many mesh systems can turn on a 2.4 GHz band, sometimes as a separate or IoT network, so check your router's settings. Your network also needs WPA2 or WPA3-Personal security. Enterprise (802.1X) networks aren't supported.

**4. Seven temperature changes a day: no, the maximum is six.**
My notes said eight periods. The spec says up to six per day. You'd need to merge two of your seven periods, for example "late" and "night." You can set a different schedule for each day of the week, and setpoints range from 5 °C to 32 °C in 0.5 °C steps.
